“Job gains remained solid and the unemployment rate stayed near its recent low,” indicating continued labor-market strength. In the literature, this is consistent with Okun’s law linking falling unemployment to above-trend real GDP. Yet inflation remains below the 2 percent objective and market-based inflation compensation is low; in New Keynesian Phillips Curve terms, anchored expectations can temper price pressures (Svensson and Woodford; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). Business fixed investment staying soft despite accommodative rates aligns with financial-frictions and collateral/“external finance premium” channels (Bernanke and Gertler; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans), which can damp capital spending even in recoveries. Holding the federal funds rate at 0.5–0.75 percent and maintaining reinvestments reflects gradualism and a Taylor-rule style reaction, while forward guidance and QE keep long rates accommodative; the literature finds QE expands the monetary base but has limited effects on real growth, justifying caution. VAR evidence on the “price puzzle” underscores monitoring of inflation indicators. Overall tone: mildly positive on growth and jobs, tempered by sub-2 percent inflation and weak capex.
